items.description:
Manual OpenSSL commands are useful for development and controlled tests. Public production services should normally automate issuance, renewal, and deployment. Choose a tool by its operational role: a GUI certificate manager, a CA/signing service, an ACME client, and a Kubernetes certificate controller solve different problems; they are not interchangeable.
For public ACME issuance, understand the challenge type:
For services that cannot be reached publicly, DNS-01 or a private CA may be appropriate. Protect DNS API credentials as production secrets.
Do not treat certificate issuance as the entire lifecycle. Renewal must be followed by validation, deployment, reload, and monitoring.

items.description: The list below is intentionally broad. A tool can be useful without being a runtime dependency or a recommendation for every deployment. Status notes were checked on 15 November 2026; upstream release cadence can change, so verify the project's releases, security policy, and supported Go versions before adopting it.

children.title: XCA
children.description: (downloads) Desktop X.509/PKI manager. Manage keys, CSRs, certificates, templates, CRLs and a small CA through a GUI. Useful when a person needs to inspect or author certificate material without building a CA workflow by hand. Not an ACME automation service. The upstream download page lists XCA 2.9.0.

repo_info.description: X Certificate and Key management

children.title: CFSSL
children.description: PKI/TLS toolkit. CLI and HTTP API for signing, verifying, bundling and inspecting certificates. Restored from the original list; it is actively releasing (v1.7.1 was published in October 2026) and the current repository states Go 1.27+ is required to build.

repo_info.description: CFSSL: Cloudflare's PKI and TLS toolkit

children.title: Smallstep
children.description: Private CA service. Useful for internal PKI, ACME-compatible issuance and managed identities.

repo_info.description: 🛡️ A private certificate authority (X.509 & SSH) & ACME server for secure automated certificate management, so you can use TLS everywhere & SSO for SSH.

children.title: mkcert
children.description: Local development CA. Convenient trusted certificates for developer workstations; do not distribute its CA private key.

repo_info.description: A simple zero-config tool to make locally trusted development certificates with any names you'd like.

children.title: minica
children.description: Minimal local CA. Useful for tests and simple local certificate chains, not a complete production PKI.

repo_info.description: minica is a small, simple CA intended for use in situations where the CA operator also operates each host where a certificate will be used.

children.title: zlint
children.description: actively maintained X.509 certificate linter for RFC, CA/Browser Forum and other PKI requirements; v3.7.2 was released in September 2026. It checks certificate profile conformance, not whether a deployment's trust model is correct.

children.title: gocertifi
children.description: embedded Mozilla-derived root bundle for environments where Go cannot find an appropriate system bundle or a pinned CA set is a deliberate requirement. Do not add it by default: an embedded root set needs an explicit update and rollout policy.

children.title: secure

children.description: certificate/public-key pinning for Apple-platform client applications. Not a Go server library. Pinning creates an outage risk when keys rotate; use only with a documented threat model, backup pins and a recovery channel.

items.description:
The original README accumulated links over many years. They are not all equally current, and a historical link should not silently become a current security recommendation.
This classification is not a judgment that the projects have no historical value. It prevents readers from confusing protocol education, old recipes, monitoring utilities, and production dependencies.
